description: Compare the experimental persistent S2 contact-impulse cache against contact-cold rebuildable sparse MPM on identical moving-bowl rollouts.

protocol.reference: Contact-cold S2 with 100 iterations, separately for each voxel size.
protocol.latency_includes: Two simulation substeps, bowl motion, swept rigid projection, diagnostic snapshots, and rebuild-status checks; rendering and policy computation are excluded.
protocol.trial_interpretation: Three repeated timings with randomized case order, using the same deterministic particle initialization; they are not independent material realizations.

monitoring.cpu_compilation_hold: The other workflow held new CPU compilation during the three accepted paired trials.

interpretation: At fixed sweep counts the cache costs approximately the same frame time in this scene; its benefit is lower rollout error at a smaller iteration budget.

At h=0.08, cached GS5 is about 1.32 times faster than contact-cold GS20 and has lower endpoint position RMS error (2.52 cm versus 2.96 cm). At h=0.12 the corresponding ratio is about 1.26 (2.37 cm versus 4.31 cm).
Cached GS2 increases final kinetic energy substantially at h=0.08 (53.25 J versus the contact-cold 100-sweep reference 32.50 J); it is not a generally validated setting.

The contact-cold 100-sweep result is a numerical comparison target, not physical ground truth. Cached GS100 differs from that target by approximately 1.2-2.0 cm, so endpoint error alone does not establish physical accuracy.
The packing law is disabled in the primary runs; its packing-excess proxy is therefore unavailable rather than zero.
All 48 accepted performance case records passed endpoint containment. This two-second check does not certify arbitrary-duration containment or continuous collision correctness.
The tested cache configuration reserves 1163268 additional cache bytes; the legacy impulse warm-start field is omitted for cache-enabled solvers.

In the separate critical_fraction=1 quality probe, cached GS20 gives packing-excess proxy 0.535 versus contact-cold GS20 0.583 and contact-cold GS100 0.532 at h=0.08. At h=0.12 it gives 0.366 versus 0.330 and 0.359 respectively. Approaching the reference can increase or decrease this proxy; it is not a measure of physical volume conservation.

eager_graph_validation.reason: This run checks replay correctness while other CPU work may proceed; eager timings are intentionally omitted.

reproduce: uv run --extra dev asv/benchmarks/simulation/bench_mpm_low_iterations.py --cases reference gs2 gs5 gs20 s2_cache100 s2_cache2 s2_cache5 s2_cache20 --particle-radius 0.036 --cell-capacity 1024 --voxel-sizes 0.08 0.12 --paired --frames 120 --critical-fraction 0 --seed SEED --output /tmp/mpm-contact-cache-SEED.json --state-output /tmp/mpm-contact-cache-SEED.npz
Repeat with SEED=42,43,44; remove --paired and add --no-cuda-graph for eager replay validation.

packing_law_diagnostic.reason: Other CPU kernel compilation may overlap; only deterministic state metrics are retained.
